incidents.vector: A cybersecurity incident affecting the school's ICT systems forced a multi-day shutdown; the nature of the attack has not been confirmed.
incidents.impact: The 1,428-pupil Buckinghamshire high school sent most students home for a second day, admitting only those sitting GCSE and A-Level exams while specialists work to restore systems.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Check Point remote-access products
incidents.vector: A VPN/remote-access vulnerability in Check Point firewalls and remote-access tools, exploited since early May, is being used by the Qilin ransomware operation to breach networks.
incidents.impact: CISA gave U.S. federal agencies three days to patch the actively exploited flaw; the bug acts as a gateway to internal networks and is being leveraged for ransomware intrusions.

incidents.vector: An external third party accessed university systems and exfiltrated data; the ShinyHunters extortion group claims it stole over 40GB of material.
incidents.impact: A 'significant amount' of current and former student data was accessed, with ~455,000 unique email addresses plus names, addresses, passport numbers, ethnicities, disabilities and fee-payment details reportedly exposed; affected campuses include the UK, Malaysia and China.

incidents.vector: The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service operation targets Internet-facing devices (VPNs, firewalls) for entry, then encrypts entire networks within hours; a 90/10 affiliate split is drawing experienced operators.
incidents.impact: Now the second-most-active ransomware gang by victim count, the group has claimed at least 332 published victims since mid-2025 and more than 240 in 2026 alone; researchers tie the administrator to an individual in Izhevsk, Russia.

incidents.victim: U.S. companies, universities and other organizations (11+ U.S. firms confirmed)
incidents.vector: Large-scale espionage using stolen session tokens to authenticate without re-authentication, masked through commercial proxy and VPN infrastructure; spear-phishing with typosquatted Microsoft login pages.
incidents.impact: U.S. prosecutors charged Russian national Denis Obrezko for facilitating the campaign by buying a VPS and domains; the Russia-aligned group has harvested bulk email/files, Teams chats and Entra ID configs across NATO states, Ukraine and beyond.

incidents.vector: Email-based attacks weaponizing the patched WinRAR path-traversal flaw CVE-2025-8088 via malicious RAR archives that drop payloads into Windows Startup locations; chains deliver the GiftedCrook stealer and HTA-based espionage malware.
incidents.impact: At least two Russia-aligned clusters used the year-old flaw against military innovation centers, military formations and law enforcement, stealing credentials and documents and establishing persistent espionage footholds.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager
incidents.vector: Actively exploited zero-day CVE-2026-20245, a validation error allowing authenticated/local attackers to inject commands and execute as root; exploitation can chain from earlier Cisco SD-WAN zero-days for the required access.
incidents.impact: The seventh actively exploited Cisco SD-WAN zero-day this year; no patch or workaround is yet available, and Cisco observed limited cases where exploitation pushed configuration changes to edge devices.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of PAN-OS authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-0257 in the GlobalProtect portal and gateway, letting unauthorized attackers circumvent controls and initiate VPN connections.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed probing and a small number of established VPN sessions; the CVE was added to CISA's KEV catalog on May 29, with no lateral movement confirmed yet.

incidents.victim: Axios NPM package and downstream open-source users
incidents.vector: Compromise of the widely used Axios NPM package (downloaded ~100 million times per week), poisoning the open-source supply chain to reach downstream projects.
incidents.impact: North Korea-nexus actors likely exposed millions of downstream users; Mandiant audited detection coverage against the campaign (tracked as UNC1069), finding blind spots at the NPM postinstall dropper entry point and the C2 exit.

incidents.vector: Hijacking of BlueSky accounts since April to post pro-Kremlin and anti-Ukraine propaganda, attributed to the Russian disinformation operation known as Matryoshka.
incidents.impact: BlueSky has been suspending hijacked accounts until owners can resecure them; the activity is part of a broader Russian influence campaign also targeting Armenian and Moldovan elections.

incidents.vector: Spear-phishing campaign luring targeted WhatsApp users to click malicious links to an external site, alongside creation of WhatsApp test accounts and groups.
incidents.impact: Meta says it disrupted the NSO-linked operation and filed to hold the company in contempt for violating a 2025 U.S. court injunction barring it from targeting WhatsApp; researchers warn NSO's tools are growing more reckless.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the NûJINHA website to delete articles and disrupt online broadcasts.
incidents.impact: Iranian hackers breached the independent news agency, deleted content, disrupted broadcasts and threatened to dox and harm employees.

incidents.vector: Data stolen from an unnamed third-party service provider used by SoFi's Hong Kong division.
incidents.impact: Customer financial and securities data was stolen via the third-party provider; the scope of affected customers has not been disclosed.

incidents.vector: Abuse of an API bug to access data from ServiceNow customer instances; the flaw was reportedly exploited since at least April before being quietly patched.
incidents.impact: Hackers accessed data across customer instances, mainly affecting customers on ServiceNow's Australia platform release; the company has notified affected customers.

incidents.vector: Repeated intrusions by attackers linked to foreign governments, per a whistleblower lawsuit from IBM's former VP of threat intelligence.
incidents.impact: The suit alleges IBM and AT&T concealed multiple breaches over years from the U.S. government and made false security assurances to win and keep federal contracts.

incidents.victim: Obama White House and U.S. Space Force Instagram accounts
incidents.vector: Attackers tricked Meta's AI support assistant into resetting account passwords by requesting a reset over a VPN near the target's hometown and instructing the bot to add an attacker-controlled email address.
incidents.impact: The Instagram accounts for the Obama White House and the Chief Master Sergeant of the U.S. Space Force were briefly defaced with pro-Iranian images and messages; Meta pushed an emergency patch and said no backend database was breached.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the university's CareerConnect platform at the end of May.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole data on alumni, research staff and employers from the recruitment platform used to connect students and staff with internships and jobs.

incidents.vector: A GitHub employee installed a malicious 'Nx Console' VS Code extension that had been compromised in the upstream TanStack supply-chain attack, giving attackers access to internal systems.
incidents.impact: More than 3,800 internal GitHub repositories were exfiltrated and offered for sale on a hacking forum, forcing GitHub to rotate critical secret tokens; Grafana linked its own breach days earlier to the same TanStack incident.
